clue.text: Proposal of a seat here for Miss Bell, subject to pairing

definitions.text: Proposal of a seat here for Miss Bell, subject to pairing

blocks.clueFragment: Proposal of a seat here for Miss Bell
blocks.note: surface reading: someone offering a chair to a lady called Miss Bell
setter's reading: the song Daisy Bell, whose suitor offers her a seat on a machine built for two riders if she will marry him

explanation.surface: A formal suitor offers Miss Bell a seat, on condition that they pair off.
explanation.walkthrough: Miss Bell is Daisy Bell of the old music-hall song 'Daisy, Daisy', where the suitor promises a ride on a tandem 'made for two'.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's proposal offers Daisy a seat on a two-person pedal machine, so the seat is found on that vehicle.

clue.text: They see drinks getting out of control

indicators.note: to get out of, that is outside, another word means surrounding it

blocks.note: beers are drinks
to have control is to have hold

explanation.surface: Drunks see drinks spiralling out of control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting out of control' reads as one phrase about wild drinking; split it, and 'out of' means wrapped outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Beholders are those who look on, people who see, as in 'in the eye of the beholder'.

clue.text: Sailing ship -- possibly a cutter

blocks.note: first meaning: a fast nineteenth-century sailing vessel
second meaning: a tool that cuts, like hair or nail shears

explanation.walkthrough: A cutter is also a small sailing boat, which pulls toward a second ship; here it means anything that cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a fast tall ship of the tea trade and also a tool for trimming, which is one kind of cutting device.

clue.text: Tribunals sitting on joint suit

blocks.note: tribunals are courts
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: Tribunals convene on a shared lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'sitting on' puts the first piece above the second. Suit looks legal; here it is wooing.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit is the old word for wooing someone with marriage in mind, the same as courtship.

clue.text: A point each way

blocks.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
ST is street, a way

explanation.surface: A bet of a point each way, as on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Each way' is a betting phrase, backing a horse to win or place; here the two words give separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: East is one of the four cardinal points of the compass.

clue.text: Small paper tag attached to idol when ordered

indicators.note: once put in order, the letters of the preceding word are rearranged from how they stand

blocks.note: a tab is a small tag or label
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A tiny label is tied to a statue of a god once things are tidied.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a newspaper printed on smaller pages than a broadsheet, so a small-format paper.

clue.text: Strip for cardiac recorder?

blocks.note: surface reading: the paper strip printed by a heart monitor
setter's reading: slang for the heart is the ticker, so a heart recorder suggests the paper strip from a stock telegraph machine

explanation.surface: The paper strip from a heart monitor.
explanation.definitionFit: The paper ribbon printed by a telegraph machine with share prices is named after the ticking device, and ticker is slang for the heart.

clue.text: Pretend to have undisclosed resources in bank

blocks.note: first meaning: to deceive, as a poker player hiding a weak hand
second meaning: a steep cliff or riverbank

explanation.surface: Faking hidden funds in your bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: Bank looks financial, matching resources; it is a steep slope.
explanation.definitionFit: To bluff is to fake strength you lack, as in poker, and a bluff is also a steep headland or riverbank.

clue.text: Taking cap off, for example, for an introduction

blocks.note: first meaning: unsealing something, such as a bottle by removing its top
second meaning: a beginning or first part

explanation.surface: Doffing your hat as a way of greeting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscrewing a lid is unsealing a container, and the first part of a speech or game is its start.

clue.text: They may come stoned to social engagements

blocks.note: first meaning: fruit sold with their pits still in
second meaning: appointments to go out with someone

explanation.surface: Guests who turn up high to parties.
explanation.walkthrough: Stoned suggests drugs; it means with the stone left in.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit of the palm is sold whole with the stone inside, and the word also means arranged outings or appointments.

clue.text: Hong Kong university accepts first-class poem

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one piece sits inside the others

blocks.note: HK is the abbreviation for Hong Kong
A1 means first-class, written with I for the figure one
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A Hong Kong university takes in an excellent piece of verse.
explanation.walkthrough: First-class is A1, and crosswords often write the figure one as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a short Japanese verse form of seventeen syllables, so a kind of poem.

clue.text: Luscious plant

blocks.note: first meaning: juicy and delicious
second meaning: a plant with thick fleshy leaves that store water, such as a cactus

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one description of a lush plant, but the adjective and the noun are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means juicy and tender as an adjective, and as a noun names a fleshy water-storing plant like a cactus.

clue.text: Learner motorists are out of place in this island

indicators.note: being out of, that is outside, another word means wrapping round it

blocks.note: L is the learner-driver plate
the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motorists' club
to place something is to put it

explanation.surface: Learner drivers feel out of place on this island.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is Britain's motoring organisation, like America's AAA; 'out of place' reads as an idiom but means outside the word place.
explanation.definitionFit: Laputa is the flying island visited in Swift's Gulliver's Travels, so a fictional island.

clue.text: Towers to be equipped with new rifles

indicators.note: something new is a fresh version, so the following word is rearranged into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Watchtowers are to be issued with fresh guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Belfries are bell towers, usually on churches, so the word names a kind of tower.

clue.text: Censor obscene writer

blocks.note: blue means smutty, as in a blue joke
a pencil is a writing implement

explanation.surface: Suppress a dirty-minded author.
explanation.walkthrough: Writer looks like an author; it is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors struck out unacceptable text with a coloured crayon, so to cut material in this way is to censor it.

clue.text: Soil from foxhole

blocks.note: first meaning: the ground or dirt plants grow in
second meaning: a fox's burrow

explanation.surface: Dirt dug out of a soldier's trench.
explanation.walkthrough: Foxhole suggests a soldier's dugout; here it is literally the den of a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means ground or dirt, and is also the British name for the underground lair of a fox.

clue.text: Wrongly teach girl to be lazy

indicators.note: done wrongly, the letters are put in the wrong positions, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Educating a girl badly will make her idle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and lacking energy, close to the sense of idle or indolent.

clue.text: Each naval disaster occurs in the fall

definitions.note: the article before it is part of the link

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks things, leaving the letters of the preceding words in a jumble

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Every shipwreck seems to happen in autumn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The fall' reads as American autumn; it is a fall of snow.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sudden mass of snow and ice sliding down a mountainside, a fall of snow.

clue.text: It adds to one's standing in the W. Indies list

blocks.note: Cuba is in the West Indies
a ship that lists leans over, or heels

explanation.surface: Something that boosts your rank in the Caribbean league table.
explanation.walkthrough: Standing suggests status; it means height while standing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a moderately high, broad shoe heel, which makes the wearer taller when standing.

clue.text: Where to ditch the old car

definitions.text: Where to ditch the old car

blocks.clueFragment: Where to ditch the old car
blocks.note: surface reading: a ditch beside the road where a motorist might crash an old vehicle
setter's reading: to ditch means to discard, and a worn-out vehicle ends up dumped on a pile of junk

explanation.surface: Somewhere to dump or crash an ageing car.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile of discarded metal and rubbish is where unwanted things, including old vehicles, are thrown away.

clue.text: Iris the first to come into flower on a Mediterranean coast

indicators.note: the first means only the opening letter of the preceding word is used
coming into something means going inside it

blocks.note: a flower here is something that flows
the opening letter of Iris
taken as written

explanation.surface: An iris is the first to bloom on the French coast.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower looks like a bloom, matching iris; read it as 'flow-er', something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Riviera is the stretch of coast along southern France and north-west Italy on the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Order 5 ac not to improvise

indicators.note: the word not removes the two letters it names from the earlier entry
to order letters is to arrange them afresh, so the remainder is rearranged

blocks.note: the answer to 5 across

explanation.surface: A command to an earlier answer not to make things up.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TO out of TABLOID, leaving ABLID, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to speak or perform without preparation, which is what improvising means.

clue.text: You can easily put your foot in it here

definitions.text: You can easily put your foot in it here

blocks.note: surface reading: the idiom for making a tactless blunder
setter's reading: literally placing a foot in a space, as in a car or plane seat with room to stretch

explanation.surface: A place where blunders come easily.
explanation.definitionFit: The space in front of a seat allows passengers to stretch out their lower limbs comfortably.

clue.text: Bill, a journalist, drew one's attention

blocks.note: a bill is a poster, an advertisement
ED is short for editor, the stock journalist

explanation.surface: Bill, a reporter, caught someone's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name; it is a printed notice or poster.
explanation.definitionFit: To advert to a matter is to turn one's mind towards it or refer to it in speech.

clue.text: A masquerade turns up by Greek author. .

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
to masquerade is to pose

explanation.surface: A disguised figure appears next to a Greek writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek storyteller credited with the famous animal fables.

clue.text: ...as does a relation in the Detroit area

indicators.note: in says the letters are sitting inside the words that follow
carries over the previous clue's 'turns up', so these letters also read upwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue: a relative turns up in Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots link to 22 down: 'as does' means this one also turns up. Relation looks like a relative; it is a proportion.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio expresses the quantitative relation between two amounts, such as three to one.

clue.text: Bound to turn lightweight, say, when home

indicators.note: turning round makes the word that follows run backwards

blocks.note: a gram is a small unit of weight, the 'say' flagging an example
to be home is to be in

explanation.surface: Something is sure to tip a scale towards lighter when at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is a boundary or edge, and a bound is likewise a limit or border.

clue.text: The wine is in the marquee

blocks.note: first meaning: a deep red Spanish wine, often used at communion
second meaning: a large canvas shelter

explanation.surface: The drinks are set out under the big canvas at a fete.
explanation.walkthrough: Tent is an old name for a dark red sweet wine from Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large canvas shelter for events, and tent is also the name of a dark Spanish red wine.

clue.text: One glass aid to sight

blocks.note: first meaning: one lens of a pair of glasses, the singular of the eyewear word
second meaning: a striking scene or show

explanation.surface: A single lens that helps you see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aid to sight' reads as one phrase; split it after aid, and sight is a noun meaning a show.
explanation.definitionFit: The singular of the word for glasses names a single eyeglass, and it also means an impressive public sight or display.

clue.text: Myrtle has split!

blocks.note: first meaning: the spice tree, a member of the myrtle family
second meaning: past tense of cleave, to split

explanation.surface: A woman called Myrtle has left, or broken apart.
explanation.walkthrough: Myrtle looks like a woman's name; it is the plant family.
explanation.definitionFit: The spice tree belongs to the myrtle family, and the old past tense of cleave means cut apart.

clue.text: On the way back record a loud bird — a pheasant

indicators.note: coming back means the word runs from right to left

blocks.note: an EP is an extended-play record
taken as written
F is forte, the musical mark for loud
an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: Heading home, someone tapes a noisy bird, a pheasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Peacocks and peahens belong to the pheasant family, so the bird is a kind of pheasant.

clue.text: The Sandhurst general's conclusion is a lot of hot air

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
the Royal Military Academy at Sandhurst trains British army officers
the last letter of general

explanation.surface: A general's closing speech at the military academy is so much bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of hot air' suggests empty talk; it is literally a rising current of warm air. Sandhurst is Britain's officer-training academy.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a column of rising warm air used by gliders and birds, literally a mass of hot air.
